content.text: The cached PDF is stale: most section files were updated on April 12, nine days after the PDF was generated. A temporary Nix lookup found Typst 0.15.1 available, so I’m attempting one clean current-source compile to `/tmp`; this will distinguish real syntax/reference failures from the missing local toolchain declaration.

The current manuscript compiles cleanly, with all fonts embedded and no image dependencies. I found no unresolved or unused citation keys; I’m doing one final metadata pass on the bibliography because two arXiv entries render with malformed APA dates, and then I’ll hand back the stale-asset and toolchain findings.

A more serious reproducibility issue surfaced in the asset audit: the manuscript’s Data Availability section names the traces, curated dataset, and generated analysis bundle, but those paths are ignored rather than versioned. I’m checking the exact local counts and whether the evolved policy needed for the reported comparison is likewise only local.

The current Typst source compiles cleanly. The blockers are toolchain/reproducibility and stale published assets, not Typst syntax.

### Exact build validation

Command:

```bash
rtk proxy env XDG_CACHE_HOME=/tmp/keating-paper-nix-cache nix shell nixpkgs#typst -c typst compile --diagnostic-format short docs/study.typ /tmp/keating-study-current.pdf
```

Result: exit `0`, no Typst diagnostics. Nix supplied Typst `0.15.1`.

Additional checks:

```bash
rtk proxy pdfinfo /tmp/keating-study-current.pdf
```

Result: 14 pages, US Letter, PDF 1.7, Creator `Typst 0.15.1`.

```bash
rtk proxy pdftotext /tmp/keating-study-current.pdf /tmp/keating-study-current.txt
rtk proxy rg -n '\?\?|<\?\?>|\[\?\]|unknown reference|missing reference' /tmp/keating-study-current.txt
```

The search exited `1`, meaning no unresolved-reference markers were found.

```bash
rtk proxy pdffonts /tmp/keating-study-current.pdf
rtk proxy pdfimages -list /tmp/keating-study-current.pdf
```

All five fonts are embedded. No raster/image assets are used; the paper consists of Typst text, math, and native tables. Every imported/included Typst file and `docs/refs.bib` exists.

`pdfinfo` prints `Syntax Error: Suspects object is wrong type (boolean)` for both the old and newly compiled Typst PDFs, but exits `0` and parses the document. This appears to be a Poppler/Typst metadata interoperability warning, not a compile failure.

### Build-path problems

There is no repository paper task, script, or CI validation. [README.md](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/README.md:198) and [DEVELOPMENT.md](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/DEVELOPMENT.md:7) say Typst is managed by devenv, but [devenv.nix](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/devenv.nix:7) installs only Bun.

```bash
rtk proxy which typst
```

Result: exit `1`; Typst is absent from the declared/current environment.

The reproducible validation command above works, but the repository should declare Typst and a paper build/check task.

### Published PDF is stale

```bash
rtk proxy sha256sum docs/study.pdf web/public/keating-metaharness.pdf /tmp/keating-study-current.pdf
```

Results:

```text
ca4aaac...  docs/study.pdf
ca4aaac...  web/public/keating-metaharness.pdf
a267fce6...  /tmp/keating-study-current.pdf
```

The tracked web PDF is identical to the ignored stale PDF:

- Published asset: Typst 0.14.0, 13 pages.
- Current source build: Typst 0.15.1, 14 pages.
- Published PDF says author `The Keating Research Group`.
- Current source and [Paper.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/pages/Paper.tsx:42) say `Dio the Debugger`.
- Published PDF omits the engagement-timeline and reward-hacking additions now present in the source.

The website directly serves the stale tracked asset via [Paper.tsx](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/web/src/pages/Paper.tsx:50) and `llms.txt`.

### Bibliography and citations

A programmatic key comparison found all ten cited keys defined and all ten bibliography entries used:

```json
{
  "missing": [],
  "unused": []
}
```

No syntactically missing citations block compilation. Remaining issues:

- The two arXiv `@misc` records in [refs.bib](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/refs.bib:87) render as `(2026,)`, with a dangling APA comma. Their metadata otherwise matches the official [Meta-Harness](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.28052) and [Hyperagents](https://arxiv.org/abs/2603.19461) records.
- Citation groups written as `@a; @b` render as `(A); (B)`, instead of one APA group `(A; B)`.
- “In CLRS terms” in [methods.typ](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/study/sections/methods.typ:104) directly invokes CLRS without a bibliography entry.
- The retention-decay/spaced-repetition claims in [methods.typ](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/study/sections/methods.typ:19) and [limitations.typ](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/study/sections/limitations.typ:11) need a learning-science citation.
- Mastery-loop and reward-hacking references would also strengthen the manuscript, though they are less direct omissions.
- Thesen and Park supports deployment, usage, and learner perceptions, but not causal learning improvement; the sentence saying recent AI tutors show scalable benefit should either be narrowed or use stronger outcome evidence. See the [publisher article](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41746-025-02022-1).

### Reproducibility assets are not checked in

This command produced no output:

```bash
rtk git ls-files test/traces test/final_dataset.json docs/generated .keating/state/current-policy.json
```

All named study inputs/outputs are ignored:

- `test/traces/`
- `test/final_dataset.json`
- `docs/generated/`
- `.keating/state/current-policy.json`

That contradicts the manuscript’s “checked-in snapshot” and Data Availability language in [results.typ](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/study/sections/results.typ:14) and [availability.typ](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/docs/study/sections/availability.typ:7). Twenty-two local trace files exist, but a fresh clone will not contain them.

Additionally, [loadPolicy()](/home/diogenes/Projects/keating/src/core/policy.ts:99) silently falls back to `DEFAULT_POLICY` when the ignored evolved-policy file is absent, so a fresh-clone analysis cannot reproduce the claimed evolved-vs-default comparison.

The concurrently refreshed local analysis now reports:

- Policy: `me-candidate-33`
- Mean full-suite delta: `3.982`, 200/200 wins
- Evolution: `24/30` wins, mean `6.998`

The manuscript still reports `keating-candidate-22`, delta `6.703`, and `29/30` wins with mean `5.768`. Either the historical policy/results need frozen versioned inputs, or the paper needs regeneration.

I made no repository edits; validation outputs are under `/tmp`.
